verdict.rationale: Rootly AI in Slack takes actions from natural-language requests, such as updating incident severity, paging teams and converting to a private incident, and it confirms destructive actions first. The changelog adds creating overrides, looking up who's on call and creating retrospectives, and the MCP server lets agents query and act on Rootly from tools like Claude Code. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of natural-language command execution, and a documented full scope of supported actions (the web chat is read-only, so action-taking is shown mainly in Slack).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Rootly AI in Slack answers questions grounded in your Rootly data and takes actions on your behalf, confirming destructive actions before they fire.
mention @Rootly in the channel or thread and ask "catch me up" or "page the database on-call team". Rootly AI always replies in-thread.
Rootly AI can now create overrides, look up who's on call, create retrospectives, and answer questions about Rootly.
Open it on any incident and ask questions in natural language.
you can query incidents, check on-call schedules, find similar past incidents, and take action — all from within Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or any other MCP-compatible environment.
